newsitem.title: CHINA: China wants cooperation with U.S. Fed's Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: China wants cooperation with U.S. Fed's Greenspan.

text.p: China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji told visiting U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan Wednesday he hoped for greater cooperation between their two central banks, state television reported.
Greenspan arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for two days of meetings with China's most senior finance and banking officials at the invitation of the central bank, the People's Bank of China.

Vice-Premier Zhu, architect of China's economic reforms and state business restructuring, outlined details of China's financial reforms as well as its reforms of lumbering state enterprises and expressed the hope for greater cooperation between the two central banks, state television said.
On his arrival at the airport, Greenspan said he was looking forward to his two days of talks in Beijing but declined to comment further.
Greenspan, on his second visit to China, also was to hold talks with Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China.
China has been trying to give its central bank greater autonomy and diplomats say it is eager to study the methods of other central banks around the world.

On Thursday, Greenspan was to meet Chen Jinhua, chairman of the State Planning Commission as well as Finance Minister Liu Zhongli and President and Communist Party leader Jiang Zemin before leaving early on Friday for Tokyo, they said.

Chinese central bank officials said the trip was part of normal exchanges with the Federal Reserve, which has had a cooperative relationship with China's central bank for more than a decade, offering technical exchanges and training.
